'''Yair Censor''' ({{Langx|he|יאיר צנזור}}; born November 29, 1943) is an [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[mathematician]] and professor emeritus at the [[University of Haifa]], specializing in [[computational mathematics]] and [[optimization (mathematics)|optimization]], as well as applications of these fields, in particular to [[medical imaging]] and [[radiation therapy]] treatment planning.<ref name="HaifaProfile">{{cite web |title=Yair Censor |url=https://cris.haifa.ac.il/en/persons/yair-censor/ |publisher=[[University of Haifa]] |access-date=September 19, 2026}}</ref>

==Biography==
Yair Censor was born in [[Rishon LeZion]]. After serving in the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]], he studied at the [[Technion - Israel Institute of Technology|Technion]] in Haifa, where he earned his [[D.Sc.]] in 1975 under the supervision of Professor Adi Ben-Israel.

==Academic career==
Censor joined the Department of Mathematics at the University of Haifa in 1979, became [[full professor]] in 1989, and became professor [[emeritus]] in 2012.<ref name="HaifaProfile" /> His research focuses on mathematical aspects of Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy ([[IMRT]]). In 2002, he founded the Center for Computational Mathematics and Scientific Computation at the University of Haifa. In recent years he is involved with research about the Superiorization Methodology.<ref>[[Superiorization|Superiorization Methodology]]</ref>{{Circular reference|date=July 2018}}

Together with S.A. Zenios, he co-authored the book ''Parallel Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications'' ([[Oxford University Press]], New York, NY, USA, 1997), for which he received the 1999 ICS ([[INFORMS]] Computing Society) Prize for Research Excellence in the Interface Between Operations Research and Computer Science.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.informs.org/Community/ICS/Prizes/ICS-Prize |title=ICS Prizes |access-date=2011-07-12 |archive-date=2010-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101020144637/http://www.informs.org/Community/ICS/Prizes/ICS-Prize |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Active in the struggle to preserve the [[academic freedom]] of the research universities in Israel, Censor was one of the founders of the Inter-Senate Committee (ISC) of the Universities for the Protection of Academic Independence.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121007014647/http://www.weizmann.ac.il/ISC/ ISC - Inter Senate Committee of the Universities for the Protection of Academic Independence]</ref>
